Step 0

Getting Started

1

Open the Predictor

Visit paulhessle-cyber.github.io/Racer/index.html on your phone or desktop. This is the most up-to-date version and is updated regularly. No installation required — it runs entirely in your browser.

2

Load Your Model (optional but recommended)

Tap SETUP in the navigation bar. Tap the model drop zone and select your racing_model.json file. This was created by the Trainer app. Without a model, the predictor uses built-in default weights.

💡 Transfer your model file via AirDrop, WhatsApp, or email — whatever is easiest from your computer to your phone.
3

Get Your Racecard PDF

Download a racecard PDF from At The Races (ATR). These are available free on race day from their website or app. One PDF per meeting.

Step 1

Getting the Racecard & Odds

Follow these steps every race day. It takes about 60 seconds once you know the flow.

1

Open attheraces.com and find today's meeting

Go to attheraces.com, tap CARDS at the top, then tap the meeting you want. You'll see the going, weather and race list.

Tap CARDS → choose your meeting → you'll see going and race list
2

Download the PDF — tap "Racecards Only · Large view"

Scroll down to All Racecards within one PDF. Tap At The Races Racecards Only → Large view. This downloads a clean PDF with all runners, form, weights and jockeys. Save it to your Files app.

💡 Use Large view — it gives cleaner text extraction when the app reads the PDF.
3

Copy the odds — highlight from stall 1 to the last runner's price

On the ATR race page, scroll to the runners list. Press and hold on the number 1 (stall 1) until the text selection handles appear. Then drag the end handle down past the last runner's odds. You should have everything from stall 1 through to the final price selected. Tap Copy.

💡 Make sure "Use decimal odds" is ticked on the ATR page — Formintel uses decimal format.
Tick "Use decimal odds" then highlight from stall 1 all the way to the last price → Copy
4

Load the PDF into Formintel

Open Formintel. Tap RACES. Tap the dashed drop zone and select the PDF you saved. All races for the meeting appear automatically with their distances and runner counts.

All races load automatically — tap any race to go straight to the prediction screen
5

Paste the odds into Formintel

Tap a race to open it, then tap PASTE ODDS at the top right. A text box appears — tap inside it and tap Paste to paste the copied ATR text. Then tap ✓ APPLY ODDS.

Tap PASTE ODDS → paste into the box
Green bar confirms how many odds matched
6

Remove any non-runners

If a horse is a non-runner, it will show NON RUNNER in orange with an NR button. Tap NR to remove it from the race — it will be struck through and excluded from the prediction and all calculations including Lucky 15 selections.

Action Pact and Now The Eagle show as NON RUNNER — tap NR on each to remove them
7

Run the prediction

Set the going selector to match today's official going, then tap ⚡ Predict. The model ranks every runner by probability. The full predicted order appears with confidence percentages, score explanations, and a Model vs Market value chart at the bottom.

Treasure Islands ranked #1 at 31% — the green VALUE bar shows model rates it higher than the market
In this example: Formintel ranked Treasure Islands #1 (31% vs 23% market implied — a value overlay). Dreams Adozen was market favourite but ranked #2. The ▲ VALUE badge flags Treasure Islands as a potential overlay worth considering.

Reading the Predictions

Each runner is ranked by model probability. Here's what a typical result looks like:

The rank number (1, 2, 3...) is your model's order. The percentage is the model's estimated win probability. The badges explain what drove the score.

The MODEL VS MARKET section below the rankings shows where the model disagrees with the bookmaker. Green bars = model rates higher than market (potential value). Red bars = market rates higher than model (potential avoid).
Reference

Symbol & Badge Reference

Symbol Badge Meaning & When It Shows
▲ ▲ STEAM
Market Steam
The odds have shortened significantly since the market opened — money is coming in for this horse. Indicates confidence from informed bettors.
Shows when odds drift inward by more than a threshold compared to opening price.
▽ ▽ DRIFT
Market Drift
The odds have lengthened — money is going elsewhere. Can indicate the yard is not confident, horse not right, or simply the market moving to other runners.
Shows when odds move outward by a significant amount.
▶ ▶ FRONT
Front-Runner
Form analysis suggests this horse races prominently or from the front. Important at tracks where pace is decisive — front-runners dominate at Chester and Brighton, struggle at Cheltenham and Sandown.
Always shown. Based on form string analysis.
◀ ◀ CLOSER
Hold-Up / Closer
This horse tends to race from the rear and finish strongly. Particularly suited to uphill finishes (Cheltenham, Sandown, Beverley, Goodwood).
Always shown. Based on form string analysis.
💎 💎 VALUE
Value Overlay
The model rates this horse significantly higher than the bookmaker's implied probability. For example, model says 25% chance but market only implies 14% — that gap is the value.
Shows when model probability is meaningfully above market implied probability.
✈ ✈ 180mi
Long Travel Alert
The trainer's home base is 100+ miles from today's racecourse. Trainers don't make long trips without a specific reason — they believe this horse has a strong chance in this race. The number shows the approximate distance travelled.
Requires a trained model with trainerCourses data. Shows when trainer's nearest home course is 100+ miles from today's track.
👀 👀 BF
Beaten Favourite
This horse was sent off at odds-on (shorter than evens) in its last start within the past 90 days — and got beaten. This is a significant signal. The yard clearly had confidence, but something went wrong. If the horse is now available at a bigger price, it may represent excellent value.
Shows when the horse's most recent odds-on start ended in defeat, within the last 90 days. Requires a trained model.
Draw
▲▼		 Draw ▲ +18%
Draw Bias Adjustment
At certain tracks, stall position significantly affects a horse's chance. A low draw at Chester, a high draw at Beverley or Ascot's straight course. The percentage shows how much the score has been adjusted up or down based on the stall.
Shows when adjustment is ±3% or more. Covers 18 UK courses including Chester (most extreme), Beverley, Ascot, Catterick, Wolverhampton, Epsom.
Track
▲▼		 Track ▲ +9%
Track Profile Adjustment
Based on whether this horse's running style suits the course characteristics. A closer gets a bonus at uphill tracks like Cheltenham and Sandown. A front-runner benefits at tight tracks like Chester and Brighton. The model knows 35 UK courses.
Shows when adjustment is ±3% or more. Effect is scaled — full influence in sprints, reduced over 2m+ staying trips.
+% Jockey +11%
Jockey / Trainer Multiplier
35+ elite jockeys and top trainers carry score multipliers based on their win rate. William Buick, Frankie Dettori, Ryan Moore, Aidan O'Brien, John Gosden etc. A specific jockey-trainer pairing bonus also applies for 15 known successful combinations.
Shows in the score explainer when the multiplier contribution is positive.
Score explainer text — the small text below each horse name (e.g. "Market 31% · Form ▲ · Jockey +9% · Track ▲ +8%") summarises what drove the score. Market % = the bookmaker's implied probability. Each element after that is an adjustment the model applied on top.
Betting

Lucky 15

A Lucky 15 is 15 bets across 4 selections: 4 singles, 6 doubles, 4 trebles, and 1 four-fold. All races must be loaded first.

1

Load multiple meetings

Load PDFs from different meetings for the day. The Lucky 15 selects one horse from each of four different races across different meetings.

2

Set your stake and bet type

Tap LUCKY 15 in the navigation. Enter your stake per unit, choose WIN or E/W (each way), and if E/W select ¼ or ⅕ place terms to match your bookmaker.

💡 For E/W: your total stake is 30× the unit (15 win bets + 15 place bets). A £0.50 E/W unit = £15 total stake.
3

Tap ⚡ Find Best Lucky 15

The smart strategy picks one horse from each odds band — keeping the combination balanced and realistic:

Leg 1
KINGSTON HILL SHORT
Ascot 14:55 · 3.2 odds
Leg 2
SILVER ARROW MID
Goodwood 15:10 · 5.5 odds
Leg 3
GREAT DAVID LONG
Chester 13:30 · 14.0 odds
Leg 4
CAPE CORAL MID
York 16:05 · 6.0 odds
SHORT = 5/2–4s · MID = 4/1–10s · LONG = 10/1+ · Each from a different race
4

Read the Min/Max return table

The scenario table shows the actual worst and best case return for each number of winners — not a probability-weighted average. "3 winners: £74 – £607" means the worst 3-winner combination returns £74 (all 3 short ones won) and the best returns £607 (including the long shot).

5

Save as Bet

Tap 💾 Save as Bet at the bottom of the card. A file downloads automatically. Import it into the Results Dashboard → Bets tab to track your P&L after the races.

Accuracy Tracking

Logging Results

1

After a race finishes

Scroll down on any prediction page — below the Model vs Market chart there is a 📋 LOG THE RESULT section. Select the finishing positions from the dropdowns.

2

Place terms are automatic

The number of position dropdowns adjusts automatically based on field size:

  • 2–4 runners: 1st only (win-only race — no place betting)
  • 5–7 runners: 1st and 2nd (2 places)
  • 8+ runners: 1st, 2nd, and 3rd (3 places)
💡 A result only counts as a "place" if the field has 5+ runners. A top pick finishing 2nd in a 4-horse race is logged as a loss — which is the correct standard.
3

Export your results

After logging, tap ⬇ Export Results JSON. This downloads all your logged races as a file. Import it into the Results Dashboard to see your full accuracy analysis.

💡 The log is stored on your device — export regularly as a backup. Each export adds to the existing log, not replaces it.
Analysis

Results Dashboard

Open the Results Dashboard and import your exported JSON file to access five tabs:

TabWhat it shows
Overview Win%, place%, loss%, best streak, average winner rank, and a running P&L curve comparing your model's top pick against backing the market favourite every race.
Backtesting Simulate different betting strategies on your logged races. Filter by confidence%, odds range, and value-only. Finds the optimal confidence threshold for maximum ROI. Shows P&L by odds band.
Race Log Full list of every logged race with win/place/loss filter. Shows confidence, odds, top pick, actual winner, and where the winner ranked in your predictions.
Bets 💰 Track Lucky 15 and Placepot bets. Import bet files saved from the predictor. Calculates actual returns automatically for Lucky 15s. Shows P&L over time for each bet type.
Insights 🔬 Retrain suggestions based on your logged results. Analyses win rate by distance, going, odds range, confidence band, and course. Flags where the model over or underperforms and which feature to adjust.
Advanced

Building Your Own Model

The Trainer is optional. The predictor works without a custom model using built-in default weights. A custom model improves accuracy by learning from historical UK/Ireland race results.
1

Get the training data

Download the UK/Ireland racing dataset from Kaggle: deltaromeo/horse-racing-results-ukireland-2015-2025. This is free and covers 10 years of UK and Irish racing results.

2

Open the Trainer and set filters

Open the Trainer app. Set Surface to 🌿 Turf, Date Range to 2020–2026, and Origin to 🇬🇧 UK & Ireland Only. This filters out older and international data that is less relevant to today's UK racing.

3

Load the CSV and train

Load the CSV file and tap Train Model. Training takes a few minutes. When complete, tap ⬇ Download Model to save racing_model.json.

4

Load into the Predictor

Transfer the model file to your phone (AirDrop, WhatsApp, email). In the Predictor, tap SETUP and load the file. The model pill in the header changes from "NO MODEL" to show accuracy stats.

💡 After loading 30+ race results, go to SETUP → Calibrate Now. This analyses your logged results and adjusts the model's confidence scores to better match real-world outcomes.
